mappings.note: Asks who wrote 'मनुष्यता' -- authorship identification, which neither LO-4 (काव्यबोध) nor LO-5 (भाव/कला) covers, so the literature competency. (Its key is wrong: the flagged option is जयशंकर प्रसाद; reported separately.)
Whom the phrase 'अमर्त्य-अंक' is used for (the gods' lap). Construing the poem's Sanskritised compound is कला-पक्ष, hence LO-5 rather than LO-4.
Who stands in the sky (असंख्य देवता). A detail of the poem, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
Who broke ancient conventions (महात्मा बुद्ध) -- one of the poem's exemplars. Content recall, LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Whom the poet counts as a man (the परोपकारी). A proposition of the poem, so LO-4, not a gloss under LO-5.
According to what we receive our fruit (our own deeds). Content of the poem, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Which man is like an animal (one who thinks only of himself). Stated proposition, so LO-4; the item asking what 'पशु प्रवृत्ति' means is the LO-5 one.
Who worships the generous man (all creation). Content recall, LO-4 rather than LO-5.
How we should advance -- pushing aside the obstacles on the way. A prescription the poem states, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
How to walk the chosen path (joyfully). Drawn from 'सहर्ष खेलते हुए', so LO-4; the gloss of 'अभीष्ट मार्ग' is separately LO-5.
Who the poet calls a true man (one who works for others' good). Proposition of the poem, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Who stands in the endless sky (असंख्य देवता). Content recall, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Who donated his bones to save the gods (महर्षि दधीचि). The poem's allusion as fact, LO-4 and not LO-5.
What man should never fear (मृत्यु). A proposition of the poem, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Whose praise the world sings -- the one who spreads unity and wholeness. Content, LO-4 and not LO-5.
What the poet names as the greatest capital (सहानुभूति). A stated claim, so LO-4; the item asking the भाव of that same line is LO-5.
What one must never be proud of (wealth). Proposition of the poem, LO-4 rather than LO-5.
The greatest अनर्थ in this world -- a brother not relieving a brother's pain. Content of the poem, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
Which kind of man makes the earth blessed (the उदार). A stated claim; the item asking the आशय of 'धरा कृतार्थ भाव मानती है' is the LO-5 one.
Who gave his flesh for a pigeon (राजा शिवि). The allusion recalled as fact, LO-4 and not LO-5.
What is to be pushed aside on the chosen path (विपत्ति और विघ्न). Content of the line, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
आशय of 'तरते हुए तरें' -- rising oneself while helping others rise. Construal of a quoted phrase, hence LO-5 and not LO-4.
When our death counts as सुमृत्यु. The poem's coined term has to be construed, so LO-5, in line with the other सुमृत्यु items; LO-4 covers plain facts.
Who never dies (one who lives for others). Stated proposition, LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Who tells the tale of generous men (सरस्वती). A detail from the poem, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
What Dadhichi sacrificed for society (his bones). The allusion as narrative fact, LO-4 rather than LO-5.
What Karna gave away (कवच and कुंडल). Content of the poem's allusion, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
What Buddha achieved by compassion (silencing all opposition). A fact the poem states, LO-4; the line-explication item covering the same couplet is LO-5.
Why Dadhichi is remembered -- he gave his bones for the destruction of the asuras. Narrative reason, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Who is a true man per the poet (one who lives and dies for humanity's good). Proposition of the poem, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Whom the poet holds the real man (all of: binds the world in brotherhood, cares for others, is compassionate). Content, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Meaning of the word 'उशीनर' (King Shivi of Gandhar). A gloss on the poem's proper-noun diction, so LO-5; the item asking what Ushinar did is LO-4.
Why the poet asks everyone to move as one -- welfare, goodwill, no discrimination. Reasons the poem gives, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
Who Gupta's father was. कवि-परिचय, which neither LO-4 nor LO-5 reaches, so the literature competency.
What Gupta's poetic subject matter presents (a golden picture of India's past). A judgement about his whole oeuvre, not about this poem, so C-H2.3 rather than LO-5.
Which languages Gupta commanded equally (Braj and Sanskrit). A fact about the poet, so the competency; LO-5 is reserved for the language of the poem itself.
Whom the poet calls 'स्वयंभू'. Identifying the referent of a Sanskrit epithet in the poem, so LO-5 and not LO-4.
What the poet counts as 'बाह्य भेद' -- difference arising from कर्म and धर्म. Construing the poem's own term, so LO-5 rather than the factual LO-4.
What inspiration the gods give man (to come to their realm). Content of the poem, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Which lines advise a life without pride -- locating the couplet in the text. Recall, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Which language influences Gupta's poetry (Sanskrit). It sits in the कवि-परिचय block and speaks of his corpus, not of this poem's कला-पक्ष, so C-H2.3 rather than LO-5.
Names of Gupta's major works (साकेत, यशोधरा, जयद्रथ वध). Bibliographic, so the literature competency and not the poem-bound LOs.
Who Gupta's younger brother was (सियारामशरण). कवि-परिचय again, hence C-H2.3.
How a generous man is recognised (by his benevolent, humble conduct). A proposition of the poem, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
What message the poet gives for मनुष्यता. The poem's burden as a whole is its भाव-पक्ष, hence LO-5 and not the particular-fact outcome LO-4.
What the poet urges on everyone (to walk as one). A specific prescription rather than the poem's overall संदेश, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
What kind of life one should live (परोपकारी, सर्वहितकारी). Content of the poem, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Meaning of 'क्षितीश' (= राजा). Word gloss on the poem's Sanskritised diction, so LO-5 rather than LO-4. It is a शब्दार्थ item, not a व्याकरण rule, so not C-H2.2 either.
Meaning of 'मदांध' (= blind with pride). A gloss on the poem's word, hence LO-5; C-H2.2 would be right only for a sandhi/samas/upasarg operation on it.
Which great men books praise (those who do good to others). A claim the poem makes, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
How Ushinar saved the pigeon (by giving his own flesh). Narrative content of the allusion, so LO-4 -- the item asking what 'उशीनर' means is LO-5.
What should be in man's heart (करुणा and दया). A proposition of the poem, LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Why no one is अनाथ -- all share one divine father. The reason is stated in the poem, so LO-4; the gloss of 'सनाथ होना' is the LO-5 item.
Why the gods stand in the sky (to applaud those who do good). Content of the poem, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
What all men are per the poet (भाई-बंधु). Recall of the claim; the item asking the अभिप्राय of 'मनुष्य मात्र बंधु है' is the LO-5 one.
Whom God stays with (the compassionate). Proposition of the poem, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
The poem's chief example of one who had God with him (महात्मा बुद्ध). Content recall, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Why Buddha is still remembered (his compassion). A reason the poem supplies, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
How the poet says we should advance (by mutual cooperation). Content of the poem, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Asks the प्रतिपाद्य / मूलभाव of the whole poem in about 100 words. The central emotive burden is भाव-पक्ष, so LO-5 rather than LO-4's particular facts.
